drivers: Recovery balance is suppressed (not quantified in data but implied by disproportionate Z4 zone dominance this month — 31% vs 8% last month — without corresponding HRV or sleep metrics to offset load), ACWR likely elevated (no acute/chronic TRIMP values provided, but this month’s 6 runs + 31% Z4 volume on only 29.5 km suggests high-intensity density), resting HR trend rising (avg HR increased from 134 bpm in Aug to 139 bpm in Sep despite slower avg pace), aerobic TE worsened (3.0 vs 2.6), and no sleep or HRV baseline data available to confirm resilience
readiness.guidance: Prioritise recovery actions over volume or intensity gains for the next 7–10 days.

monthly_review.summary: September shows a sharp shift toward higher-intensity running with declining efficiency and pacing control, contrasting with August’s higher-volume, lower-intensity base-building focus.
monthly_review.highlight: Z4 zone representation surged to 31% this month (vs 8% last month and 18% in July), indicating a rapid, unbalanced shift into threshold work without sufficient recovery support or prior aerobic consolidation.

goal_tracker.message: To match last month’s 51.3 km, 21.8 km across 4 remaining sessions would require ~5.5 km/session at unsustainable intensity given compromised readiness; chasing this target risks injury or burnout and is not advisable.

insights.title: Threshold overload without aerobic buffer
insights.body: Z4 volume jumped to 31% this month (29.5 km total) — equivalent to ~9.2 km in Z4 — while Z1 dropped to 26% (vs 43% in Aug). This occurred alongside a 0.44 ml/kg/km worsening in running economy and +0.4% aerobic decoupling, suggesting insufficient Z1/Z2 volume to support Z4 adaptation.

insights.title: Cadence collapse correlates with fatigue markers
insights.body: Cadence fell from 149 spm (Aug) to 136 spm (Sep), and recent long run (9/6, 10.7 km) showed cadence of only 90 spm — lowest in recent runs — coinciding with highest aerobic TE (5.0%) and elevated HR (158 bpm), indicating neuromuscular fatigue compromising stride integrity.

insights.title: Pace improved but HR rose disproportionately
insights.body: Avg pace improved (+10 sec/km) while avg HR increased +5 bpm — unusual for aerobic development — and best pace (369 sec/km = 6:09/min) appeared in a short, unmeasured-effort session (9/3, 1.0 km), suggesting reliance on anaerobic capacity rather than sustainable aerobic speed.

insights.title: Worsening efficiency aligns with missing recovery metrics
insights.body: Running economy declined from 13.42 (May) → 13.46 (Jun) → 13.64 (Jul) → 14.12 (Aug) → 14.56 (Sep), a consistent 0.4+ ml/kg/km monthly deterioration, yet no HRV, sleep, or resting HR trend data is provided to assess whether this reflects true physiological decay or inadequate recovery between sessions.

recommendations.action: Zone 1 run: 45 min easy, HR ≤ 125 bpm, on Tuesday — no pace target, focus on cadence ≥ 145 spm and relaxed breathing
recommendations.reason: Restores autonomic balance, counters elevated avg HR and suppressed recovery signals, and rebuilds neuromuscular coordination without load

recommendations.action: Complete 20 min guided breathwork (4-7-8 protocol) after every run this week, tracked via Garmin Body Battery — stop if Body Battery drops < 30 post-session
recommendations.reason: Directly addresses compromised readiness by supporting parasympathetic reactivation, especially critical given missing HRV/sleep confirmation and rising aerobic TE

recommendations.action: Replace one scheduled run with 30 min mobility + foam rolling (focus: glutes, hip flexors, calves), no cardio — log as 'active recovery' in Garmin
recommendations.reason: Mitigates cadence drop and ground contact time increase (389 ms on 9/1, up from 282–292 ms in faster efforts), reducing mechanical strain risk

risk_flags.evidence: Z4 zone % up 31% (vs 8% last month), aerobic TE up 0.4%, avg HR up 5 bpm, cadence down 13 spm, running economy up 0.44 ml/kg/km — all trending negatively across 2 months without recovery metric improvement
risk_flags.action: Pause all Z4+ work for 10 days; retest Z4 tolerance only after 3 consecutive days of HRV within 5% of July baseline (unavailable, so use avg HR ≤ 132 bpm + aerobic TE ≤ 2.6 as proxy)

risk_flags.evidence: Ground contact time spiked to 389 ms (9/1) and 385 ms (8/23) — >370 ms consistently — while vertical oscill rose to 9.2 (9/3), and cadence fell below 140 spm in 4 of last 5 runs
risk_flags.action: Introduce barefoot calf raises (2x20 daily) and single-leg balance drills (3x60 sec/day) to reinforce neuromuscular control before reintroducing sustained running

weekly_focus.description: Shift emphasis from output (pace, distance, zones) to input control (HR, cadence, breath, ground contact) to interrupt fatigue-driven gait degradation and restore parasympathetic tone.
suggested_sessions: Short technique-focused strides (6x20 sec, walk 60 sec, focus on light footstrike and cadence ≥ 150)
